passages.text: The theme of the Vedanta is to see the Lord in everything, to see things in their real nature, not as they appear to be.
passages.note: Seeing the sacred in ordinary things

passages.text: You may invent an image through which to worship God, but a better image already exists, the living man. You may build a temple in which to worship God, and that may be good, but a better one, a much higher one, already exists, the human body.
passages.note: Honouring the divine in living people

passages.text: There are cases where truth is not comfortable until we reach its climax. Human nature is very conservative It does something, and having once done that, finds it hard to get out of it. The mind will not receive new thoughts, because they bring discomfort.
